title: Reconciliation decision log entry
description: One JSON object per line in decisions.jsonl. Append-only: never edit or delete a line. To change a decision, append a new one with supersedes set to the old id. Replaying the file in order reproduces the reconciliation exactly.

actor.description: Who made the call. 'user' is a human judgement; 'agent' is model-proposed; 'engine' is computed deterministically.

kind.description: Closed vocabulary. If a needed decision does not fit one of these, do not invent a new kind - raise it as an open question instead.

statement.description: The decision content. Shape depends on kind; keys stay in English.

reason.description: Why this decision was made, in the user's language. Mandatory - a decision without a reason is not auditable.

evidence.description: Concrete figures supporting the decision: amounts, row counts, keys, file hashes, rule coverage.

confidence.description: See references/confidence.md. A decision resting on an unconfirmed assumption cannot exceed that assumption's confidence.

impact.description: Effect on the reconciliation, when known.

supersedes.description: id of the decision this replaces, if any.

run_id.description: Run in which this decision was first applied.

examples.reason: Tested both conventions across all shared keys; subtraction reconciled 867 accounts versus 12 for addition.
Loan accounts are maintained in the treasury system and are out of scope for this sub-ledger reconciliation.
The two sibling accounts show gaps that offset exactly, so the value was posted to the wrong sub-account rather than being missing.
